title: Derive a contract decision's settled status without writing to the trigger store
action:
Per D1 and D2 (plan.md, Approach, S3): a contract's settled status is a DERIVED view over the decision log - no new store, no registry, no reverse index. This cell builds the read only. It adds no guard and refuses nothing; the tripwire that consumes it is the next cell.

Step 1 - a read-only trigger reader. read_and_evaluate (verbs/triggers/mod.rs:223) is the only reader and it WRITES: for a predicate-tier trigger still waiting whose predicate is true, it flips status to due and calls write_json_atomic (mod.rs:249-251). A refusal path that promises zero mutation cannot call it. Refactor rather than copy: extract the directory walk and record parse into ONE shared body that takes a flag for whether the predicate flip is performed, then express read_and_evaluate as that body with the flip ON and a new pub(crate) read-only entry point as the same body with the flip OFF. Two copies of this walk would be two things that can disagree; the learned pattern 'A rule checked at two points needs one shared read' is exactly this case. Keep the existing fail-open behaviour in both: a missing directory is empty, a raced-away file is skipped, a corrupt or shape-invalid file becomes Unreadable rather than a crash.

Step 2 - the status read, in verbs/decisions/read.rs beside active_decisions (:146). Add a pub(crate) function that answers, for one decision id: settled when the id is in the active decision set AND no trigger keyed to it has status waiting or due; unsettled when it is in the active set AND such a trigger exists; unknown when it is not in the active set at all. 'Unknown' is the plan's resolution of D3's word 'retired': the store has no retired state, only supersession (read.rs:156), redaction (:162) and archiving, and all three drop the id out of active_decisions, which is exactly the condition to refuse on later. Use the read-only reader from step 1, never read_and_evaluate.

Step 3 - the join is on SHORT8, not on the full id. TriggerRecord.decision holds the first 8 characters of the decision id (verbs/triggers/mod.rs:75-85, written at :402). Match by comparing the record's decision against the first 8 chars of the id being asked about. Two live facts to honour: 4 of the 14 trigger records in this repo carry a decision key that is not a short8 at all ('herding-', 'P72', 'p-c6e61d', 'wayfindi'), so a junk key must simply match nothing rather than error; and a manual-tier trigger never reaches due (mod.rs:262-266), so a contract decision with a waiting manual trigger stays unsettled until a human resolves it - that is correct under D2, and the function's own doc comment must say so plainly.

Step 4 - a citation resolver, also a pure read, in the same place. cell.decisions does NOT hold store decision ids: measured over the 92 live cells, 81 citations, only 11 resolve, and the entry-length histogram is {2: 61, 3: 5, 8: 11, 24: 1, 25: 3} - the field is dominated by local D-IDs like 'D1' from a CONTEXT.md table (plan.md, Discovery 5). Add a pub(crate) function that maps one cell.decisions entry to Some(store decision id) or None: an exact id match resolves; a prefix of at least 8 characters that matches EXACTLY ONE active decision resolves; anything shorter than 8 characters, and any prefix matching two or more decisions, resolves to None. None means 'not a store citation' and is not an error - the next cell passes over it silently.

Step 5 - tests in verbs/decisions/tests.rs, over fixture stores built in a tempdir; judge existing coverage first and author only the gap. From plan.md's test matrix: settled, unsettled-waiting, unsettled-due, and unknown-because-superseded each derived correctly; a resolved trigger leaves the decision settled; a manual waiting trigger leaves it unsettled; a trigger file with a junk decision key matches nothing; two decision ids sharing a short8 do not borrow each other's trigger; a corrupt trigger file degrades rather than panics; the trigger files are BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after the read-only reader runs over a predicate-tier waiting trigger whose predicate is true (this is the load-bearing one - assert file bytes, not status); the resolver returns None for 'D1', Some for a full id, Some for a unique 8-char prefix, and None for an ambiguous prefix.

Step 6 - extend docs/knowledge/areas/decision-memory/overview.md with the derived status rule: the three values, the short8 join, the manual-trigger consequence, and the fact that nothing is stored. Do not restate the tag rule the previous cell already added there; point at it.

truths: A decision tagged for a contract with no waiting or due trigger reads as settled; one with a waiting or due trigger reads as unsettled; a superseded, redacted or archived one reads as unknown
Running the read-only trigger reader leaves every file under .bee/triggers byte-identical, even when a predicate-tier waiting trigger's predicate is true
A trigger record whose decision key is not a short8 of any decision matches nothing and raises no error
A cell.decisions entry shorter than 8 characters resolves to no store decision, and that is not an error
